title: Interpretability-Guided Auditing for Clinical Language Models for Discharge Prediction
abstract: arXiv:2611.18626v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Clinical natural language processing (NLP) models for hospital discharge prediction are vulnerable to explicit discharge-related lexical cues in clinical notes, even when note timestamps are temporally filtered. These cues may act as proxies for future outcomes, leading models to rely on shortcut-like signals rather than clinically meaningful evidence. We propose AuditBERT-Discharge, a lightweight framework that reframes interpretability as a training-time auditing mechanism. Token-level SHAP attributions from an initial BioClinicalBERT model are used to identify highly attributed discharge-related tokens, which are subsequently masked in the training corpus before model retraining. We evaluate the framework on a retrospective cohort of elective spine surgery encounters from a single academic medical center. translated_title: 面向出院预测的临床语言模型可解释性引导审计
translated_abstract: 用于医院出院预测的临床自然语言处理（NLP）模型容易受到临床笔记中明确的出院相关词汇线索的影响，即使对笔记时间戳进行了时间过滤。这些线索可能充当未来结果的代理，导致模型依赖类似“捷径”的信号，而非具有临床意义的证据。我们提出了AuditBERT-Discharge，这是一个轻量级框架，将可解释性重新构建为训练阶段的审计机制。该框架利用初始BioClinicalBERT模型的词元级SHAP归因来识别归因度高的出院相关词元，并在模型重新训练之前将这些词元从训练语料库中掩蔽。我们在某单一学术医疗中心的选择性脊柱手术就诊回顾性队列上对该框架进行了评估。定性归因分析和初步评估表明，SHAP引导的审计减少了模型对明确出院相关线索的依赖。（注：原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 提出AuditBERT-Discharge轻量级框架，将可解释性（词元级SHAP归因）作为训练时审计机制，自动识别并掩蔽临床笔记中的出院相关词汇捷径，从而减少出院预测模型对虚假线索的依赖。
